text:
deploy-bot: Rolling out runtime v4.7.0-canary -> 12% traffic across us-west-2 :rocket:

maria: saw spikes in p50/p99 for text-generation on canary slice, alerting via grafana -> https://grafana/redwood/d/runtimes

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED #INC-2026-4872 severity=P2 - high latency on runtime canary. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

maria: paging tj (on-call) - looks like tail latency and throughput drop, a subset of hosts are falling back to generic kernel. logs attached.

maria: log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T08:21:11Z runtime[pid=4332] WARNING kernel_selector: fallback_to_generic_kernel model=redwood-ggml seq_len=2048 host=canary-5
2026-03-17T08:21:12Z runtime[pid=4332] ERROR batcher: microbatch_timeout exceeded size=1 latency_ms=812 host=canary-5
```

ben: that fallback pattern matches the new kernel probe in v4.7.0 - if the specialized kernel fails, it falls back and we see huge p99. Could be a memory path regression under certain seq_len distributions.

tj: acknowledging, pulling up canary host metrics and kmsg. Can everyone avoid re-triggering rollouts? I'll coordinate mitigation.

anya: +1 from CS - two enterprise customers (org-omega, org-cascade) reported 5xx and degraded throughput for embeddings and chat since ~08:20 UTC. Est. impact: ~0.6% of overall requests but concentrated on those orgs.

maria: incident-bot, please add customer-impact annotations orgs=[org-omega,org-cascade] ci=true

incident-bot: annotations added.

tj: quick mitigation options: 1) flip feature-flag to disable new kernel probe 2) pause/rollback canary rollout 3) force-affinity to non-canary kernels. Recommending ff flip + pause.

ben: agree - ff flip first (fast), then pause rollout. ff is `runtime.canary.kprobe_v2` (default true in v4.7).

maria: tj, can you flip it? ops playbook: `rctl feature unset runtime.canary.kprobe_v2 --scope=canary`

tj: running now:
```
# from bastion
rctl feature unset runtime.canary.kprobe_v2 --scope=canary --author=tj --reason="oncall: rollback probe due to fallback"
"""
Response: feature runtime.canary.kprobe_v2 set to false for scope=canary
"""
```

maria: good. also pausing the rollout in the console.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused at 12%. No further canary slices will be promoted.

tj: watching metrics. initial note: p99 dropped from ~1.2s -> ~220ms on affected hosts. throughput recovering.

anya: confirming with CS - org-omega reports requests succeeding again. org-cascade still seeing intermittent 502s but improved.

maria: collecting logs to root cause. early hypothesis: kernel probe v2 had an edge-case for long sequence KV caching leading to OOM-ish behavior and trigger to generic kernel path. Need an isolated repro on canary-5.

ben: tagging runtime/repro owners. we should schedule a quick postmortem and decide whether to ship v4.7.0 with kprobe_v2 disabled or fix and re-enable. Also run a canary with traffic-slice=small seq_len workloads.

tj: handing off to ben for follow-up investigator shift. I'll stay on pager for 30m.

ben: taking over. next actions: 1) collect heap/stack traces from canary hosts 2) run stress tests with seq_len=2k/3k 3) get a quick patch for probe guard if repro.

maria: update incident channel when root cause confirmed. For now incident severity remains P2 but customer-impact flagged.

ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-4872 in Jira: https://jira/redwood/browse/INC-2026-4872

anya: noted. CS will keep org-omega/org-cascade updated and offer warm-start support if needed.

tj: summary for handoff to ben: ff runtime.canary.kprobe_v2 disabled at 08:25, rollout paused, p99 improved, two tenants impacted with recovery in progress. logs and traces collected under /var/log/runtime/canary-5.

ben: ack, will open a follow-up thread for root cause. thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: incident closed as active-mitigation at 08:45 UTC - monitoring. will escalate to P1 if regression returns.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: state=mitigated mitigations=[ff_disabled, rollout_paused] assigned_to=ben

ben: quick TODOs post-incident: - repro and fix kernel probe - add unit/integration tests for large-seq KV behavior - add automatic rollback condition if fallback_rate > 5% within 5m - run targeted canary with synthetic seq_len distribution

maria: agreed. closing thread for the live-handoff. please keep Jira updated.
